html:
Birka was a Viking-age trading town on the island of Björkö in Lake Mälaren, west of present-day Stockholm, from about 750 to about 975.

Furs, iron and slaves from the north and east were traded here for silver, glass, silk and weapons. Graves at Birka hold Arab silver coins, Chinese silk and Frankish glass, signs of the eastern routes used by the Varangians and of the silver that flowed from Central Asia. A grave once thought to hold a male warrior was shown by DNA in 2017 to be a woman's.

The Frankish missionary Ansgar came here about 830, the first Christian mission to Sweden. Birka was abandoned in the late 900s, perhaps as the waters fell, and Sigtuna took its place. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. See Sweden.
sum: Birka was a Viking-age trading town on the island of Björkö in Lake Mälaren, west of present-day Stockholm, from about 750 to about 975.
